Examining Cashflow Against Procter & Gamble Hygiene and Health Care's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Procter & Gamble Hygiene and Health Care recorded an accrual ratio of 0.36. Therefore, we know that it's free cashflow was significantly lower than its statutory profit, raising questions about how useful that profit figure really is. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of ₹7.2b, which is significantly less than its profit of ₹7.77b. Procter & Gamble Hygiene and Health Care's free cash flow actually declined over the last year, but it may bounce back next year, since free cash flow is often more volatile than accounting profits.

data.title: Everpure (EVRP) Stock Climbs As Q3 Results Back Margin Strength
data.description:
Everpure entered this Q3 2027 report with a punchy story on paper: high earnings growth, a rich P/E of 117.6x, and a share price that had fallen 16.6% over the past month. Then the quarter hit. Revenue reached US$1.46b and net income came in at US$100.4m, and the stock jumped 4.7% to US$105.46 in Thursday trading.

The reaction looks like relief mixed with renewed conviction. A business priced for perfection is now trying to prove that its margin strength and cash generation can support that kind of valuation.

Love Everpure’s margin story but uneasy about paying a 117.6x P/E for it? Compare this quarter with a curated 34 high quality undervalued stocks to see what stronger value-for-money combinations look like.

Q3 2027 Earnings Summary

  • Revenue, Q3 2027 vs Q3 2026: US$1,459.8m vs. US$964.5m (up 51%)
  • Net Income, Q3 2027 vs Q3 2026: US$100.4m vs. US$54.8m (up 83%)
  • Basic EPS, Q3 2027 vs Q3 2026: US$0.30 vs. US$0.17 (up 81%)
  • Total Gross Margin, Q3 2027: 69.2% (product gross margin 67.3%, subscription gross margin 72.6%)

Everpure says recent hyperscale deals carry 75–85% gross margins. Ask Charlie what makes Everpure’s hyperscale margins so rich.

Everpure’s Bull Story Meets Hyperscale Reality

The bullish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St hangs a lot on Everpure turning hyperscale wins and software into a step change in profitability.

"Hyperscale DirectFlash design wins with two top 5 cloud providers, combined with expected hyperscale shipments at 75% to 85% product gross margins and committed orders that extend through at least 2028, create potential for a re rating of Everpure's margin profile if this OEM like stream becomes a larger share of total product revenue and lifts overall gross margin."

Q3 goes a fair way toward that milestone. Product gross margin of 67.3% sat inside the 65% to 70% long term range while total gross margin reached 69.2%, with management explicitly linking part of that uplift to higher margin hyperscale deployments. Subscription still carries the richer 72.6% margin, yet hyperscale Solutions materially increased its contribution and helped deliver a record 24% operating margin alongside raised full year guidance.

That disagreement has a full argument behind it. → Uncover the higher Fair Value this Narrative argues for.

Everpure Bear Case: Cash Strain Fades, Contract Risk Lingers

Bearish analysts on Simply Wall St argue that Everpure’s growth engines could overreach and strain the balance between demand, contracts, and cash generation.

"The main thing that has to go right is that Evergreen//One, hyperscale DirectFlash deployments and AI data products such as Everpure Data Intelligence and Data Stream keep converting strong customer interest and contract value into durable, high margin revenue without overstraining cash flow or operating expenses."

Q3 edges against that concern. Revenue, operating income, and margins all improved while free cash flow reached US$265m and management still guides to US$600m to US$800m for FY27. The stress point now sits more in concentration risk and future usage optimization, since ARR of more than US$2.2b and remaining performance obligations above US$4.1b increase exposure if large customers slow deployments or renegotiate.

Zooming In On QD Laser's Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, QD Laser recorded an accrual ratio of 0.59. Statistically speaking, that's a real negative for future earnings. And indeed, during the period the company didn't produce any free cash flow whatsoever. Over the last year it actually had negative free cash flow of JP¥1.1b, in contrast to the aforementioned profit of JP¥231.0m. Coming off the back of negative free cash flow last year, we imagine some shareholders might wonder if its cash burn of JP¥1.1b, this year, indicates high risk. However, that's not all there is to consider. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.

How Do Unusual Items Influence Profit?

While it's always nice to have higher profit, a large contribution from unusual items sometimes dampens our enthusiasm. When we crunched the numbers on thousands of publicly listed companies, we found that a boost from unusual items in a given year is often not repeated the next year. And that's as you'd expect, given these boosts are described as 'unusual'. QD Laser had a rather significant contribution from unusual items relative to its profit to September 2026. All else being equal, this would likely have the effect of making the statutory profit a poor guide to underlying earnings power.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

KAON Group's profit suffered from unusual items, which reduced profit by ₩4.0b in the last twelve months. Zooming In On DTC's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

DTC has an accrual ratio of -0.17 for the year to September 2026. That implies it has very good cash conversion, and that its earnings in the last year actually significantly understate its free cash flow. In fact, it had free cash flow of ₩22b in the last year, which was a lot more than its statutory profit of ₩6.28b. Notably, DTC had negative free cash flow last year, so the ₩22b it produced this year was a welcome improvement. However, that's not all there is to consider. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.
